# @scope/demo-kit

> Sample files and a simulated agent for demos and tests of the file workspace.

- API reference: https://docs.example.invalid/api/demo-kit
- Install: `npm install --save-dev @scope/demo-kit`

## README sections

- Install
- Entry: `sampleFiles()` returns a small project to put in a memory adapter.
- Standalone use: This package has no UI, so it works with any adapter built on `createMemoryAdapter`.
- CSS: None.
- Options: `signal`: required.

## Entry points

- `@scope/demo-kit`

## Exports of `@scope/demo-kit`

- `AgentStep`: One thing the simulated agent does: `create` and `edit` write `content` to `path`, `rename` moves `path` to `to`, and `delete` removes `path`.
- `DEFAULT_AGENT_SCRIPT`: What the agent does when `simulateAgent` gets no `script`: it writes a plan, edits the README and the source, then creates, renames and deletes a scratch file.
- `DOCS_URL`: The documentation site's address, in one place so the examples, the site and the generated files agree.
- `SimulateAgentOptions`: Options of `simulateAgent`.
- `sampleFiles`: A small project tree for examples and docs: Markdown, TypeScript, JSON, CSV, an SVG, and an XLSX, a PDF and a PNG that are generated in code.
- `simulateAgent`: Plays a script of file changes against a memory adapter, one step per `intervalMs`, as if an agent were working in the project.
